title: Heavy Equipment Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.600)
subtitle: For site walks before and during work with construction machinery, mechanized equipment and vehicles.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
Record each defect and correct it before the affected work continues.
The manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Parked and unattended equipment
items: At night, beside a highway in use or near active work, unattended machines show working lights or reflectors, or stand behind barricades carrying them.
Brake applied on every parked machine.
Machines parked on an incline have chocks at the wheels and the brake applied.
Fully down on the ground or blocked whenever the machine is idle or under repair.

sections.title: Maintenance, tires, batteries and cab
items: Anything held up by slings, hoists or jacks is blocked or cribbed before anyone goes under or between it.
Controls in neutral, motor off and brakes on, unless the task needs otherwise.
Tire rack, cage or equivalent in use for inflating, mounting or dismounting split-rim or locking-ring tires.
Battery use, care and charging follow 29 CFR 1926 Subpart K.
Safety glass or equivalent fitted, with no visible distortion that affects safe operation.

sections.title: Power lines
items: Every overhead wire treated as energized unless the owner or utility has confirmed it is not and it is visibly grounded.
Every part of the crane and load stays at least 10 feet from the lines.
Distance set at 10 feet plus 0.4 inch per kV above 50 kV, or twice the insulator length, and never under 10 feet.
With no load and boom lowered: at least 4 feet under 50 kV, 10 feet above 50 kV to 345 kV inclusive, 16 feet to 750 kV inclusive.
A designated person watches clearance and warns the operator wherever it is hard to judge by sight.

sections.title: Transmitter towers and rail spurs
items: Before work near a transmitter tower, the transmitter is off or a test for induced charge on the crane has been done.
Where induced voltage must be dissipated, a ground runs directly to the upper rotating structure supporting the boom.
Jumper cables attached to materials handled by the boom when a charge is induced.
Crew has nonconductive poles with large alligator clips or similar for attaching the ground cable to the load.
No combustible or flammable materials in the immediate area when operations start.
Derail and/or bumper blocks in place where a rolling car could reach cars being worked, a building, or a work or traffic area.

references: 29 CFR 1926.600: Equipment (Part 1926 Subpart O: Motor Vehicles, Mechanized Equipment, and Marine Operations)
